凪 concerns a lull in the wind and calm conditions at sea. The noun 凪 なぎ names the calm; the verb 凪ぐ なぐ describes the wind or sea becoming calm. This is not a general translation of every English use of "calm."
Modern-shape mnemonic, not etymology: picture the outer frame of 風, "wind," with 止, "stop," inside: the wind has stopped. The indexing radical is 几, the frame, not the whole character 風.
Digital Daijisen identifies 凪 as a kokuji, a character created in Japan. The mnemonic above is a memory aid for its modern shape, not a detailed historical derivation.

Both native readings are selected for practice. In 凪ぐ, 凪 writes な and the ending ぐ stays outside the kanji. No on-reading is supplied in the source metadata.

For recognition, 朝凪 (あさなぎ) is the morning calm over the sea, and 夕凪 (ゆうなぎ) is the evening calm. These are whole-word readings.
Distinguish the noun なぎ from the dictionary-form verb なぐ: 凪です (なぎです), "it is calm at sea," versus 風が凪ぐ (かぜがなぐ), "the wind dies down."
風 concerns wind or style, not the lull itself. 凡 has a dot inside its frame and concerns the ordinary or general; 凹 describes a concave or sunken shape.
Grade 9 is the source's name-use classification, not a claim that 凪 occurs only in names. The weather noun and verb above are not names.

凪 なぎ — calm at sea; lull
凪 is a noun for a lull in the wind, especially the calm conditions at sea when the wind has died down. It names a weather condition, not a person's composure.
今日は凪です。 (きょうはなぎです。) — It is calm at sea today.
夕凪の海は静かだった。 (ゆうなぎのうみはしずかだった。) — The sea was still in the evening calm.
朝凪 (あさなぎ) means the morning calm over the sea; 夕凪 (ゆうなぎ) means the evening calm. A lull can be temporary; the word does not promise that the sea will remain calm all day.
This is one native word written with 凪, not a multi-kanji compound. The whole character writes なぎ. Compare the related verb 凪ぐ (なぐ), "become calm (wind/sea)."

穏やか (おだやか) and 静か (しずか) can describe calm sea conditions, but they are な-adjectives with broader uses. 凪 is a noun: 凪です (なぎです), rather than treating it as a な-adjective. 時化 (しけ), "stormy weather at sea," is a contrasting noun; JMdict marks that word as usually written in kana.

For a person's cool-headedness, 冷静 (れいせい) is more appropriate than using 凪 as a general equivalent of English "calm." 凪 focuses here on wind and sea conditions. To describe the change into those conditions, use 凪ぐ, not the noun alone as a verb.

凪ぐ なぐ — become calm (wind/sea)
凪ぐ is an intransitive godan verb: the wind dies down or the sea becomes calm. The wind or sea is the subject, marked with が; this is not a verb for someone actively calming another person.
夕方、風が凪いだ。 (ゆうがた、かぜがないだ。) — The wind died down in the evening.
凪いだ海は静かだった。 (ないだうみはしずかだった。) — The sea was still after it had calmed.
The ぐ ending changes as in other gu-ending godan verbs: 凪ぎます (なぎます), 凪がない (ながない), 凪いで (ないで), and 凪いだ (ないだ). In 凪いだ海 (ないだうみ), the past form describes the sea that has become calm.

凪 supplies the calm-wind/sea association and writes な; ぐ is written outside the kanji. This is one native verb, not a multi-kanji compound. The related noun 凪 is read なぎ: 凪です (なぎです), "it is calm at sea."

止む (やむ), "cease; let up," can also describe wind stopping. 静まる (しずまる), "quiet down; subside," is broader than this weather verb. Neither is an unrestricted replacement in every sentence. The noun 時化 (しけ), "stormy weather at sea," provides a contrasting condition, not an opposite verb with the same conjugation.

This article teaches the modern weather verb 凪ぐ. Dictionaries distinguish 和ぐ (なぐ), for a mind or feelings becoming calm; do not transfer the example 心が和ぐ (こころがなぐ), "one's heart becomes calm," to the ordinary weather spelling taught here. For regaining personal composure, 落ち着く (おちつく) is a useful broader comparison.
